mnemonic: 미봉 is darning a hole (봉, as in 봉합 'stitching up'); 책 is a plan (대책). The tear is stitched shut, but the fabric is still rotten.

collocations.en: to amount to no more than a stopgap

examples.ko: 전문가들은 이번 대책이 집값 불안을 잠시 덮는 미봉책에 불과하다고 지적했다.
examples.en: Experts said the measures were no more than a stopgap papering over jitters about housing prices.

examples.ko: 매번 땜질식 미봉책만 내놓지 말고 시스템 자체를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: Instead of rolling out patch-job fixes every time, we need to change the system itself.

production.promptEn: a stopgap measure; a band-aid fix

mnemonic: 묘책 = a 묘한 (uncanny, ingenious) 대책: the plan that makes everyone ask, 'Why didn't I think of that?'

collocations.en: to look for a clever fix
to have no clever way out
to come up with a clever plan

examples.ko: 인구 감소를 막을 뾰족한 묘책이 없다는 게 지자체들의 공통된 고민이다.
examples.en: What local governments share is the headache of having no clever fix for population decline.

examples.ko: 마감까지 이틀 남았는데 무슨 묘책이라도 있어?
examples.en: Two days to the deadline. Got any bright ideas?

production.promptEn: a clever solution; an ingenious plan

mnemonic: 정쟁 = 정치 turned into 전쟁: politics as a brawl. 정쟁의 도구 = a political football.

collocations.en: to get caught up in partisan fights

examples.ko: 재난 지원 문제까지 정쟁의 도구로 삼아서는 안 된다.
examples.en: Even disaster relief must not be turned into a political football.

examples.ko: 여야가 정쟁에만 몰두하는 사이 민생 법안들은 국회에서 잠자고 있다.
examples.en: While the ruling and opposition parties are busy fighting, bills that affect people's daily lives sit untouched in the National Assembly.

production.promptEn: political strife; partisan wrangling

mnemonic: 정국 = 정치 + 국면 (the state of play, as in a 바둑 대국): where all the political pieces sit right now.

examples.ko: 대통령의 거부권 행사로 정국이 급격히 얼어붙었다.
examples.en: The president's veto sent the political climate into a sudden deep freeze.

examples.ko: 총선을 앞두고 정국이 크게 요동치고 있다.
examples.en: Politics is in turmoil ahead of the general election.

production.promptEn: the political situation / climate (at a given moment)

mnemonic: 임대 has the 대 of 대출 (lending): you're the one lending your property out. 임차 has the 차 of 차용 (borrowing): you're the tenant.

examples.ko: 그는 은퇴한 뒤 상가 건물 일 층을 카페에 임대하고 있다.
examples.en: Since retiring, he's been leasing the ground floor of his commercial building to a café.

examples.ko: 청년층을 위한 공공 임대 주택 공급이 수요를 따라가지 못하고 있다.
examples.en: The supply of public rental housing for young people isn't keeping up with demand.

production.promptEn: leasing / renting OUT (the owner's side)

mnemonic: 임차 has the 차 of 차용 (borrowing): you rent the place. The landlord's side, lending it out, is 임대 (대, as in 대출).

examples.ko: 회사는 강남의 한 빌딩 두 개 층을 임차해 본사로 쓰고 있다.
examples.en: The company leases two floors of a building in Gangnam for its headquarters.

examples.ko: 계약 기간 중에 집주인이 바뀌어도 임차인의 권리는 보호된다.
examples.en: Even if the property changes hands mid-lease, the tenant's rights are protected.

production.promptEn: leasing / renting FROM someone (the tenant's side)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; 借 = borrow; legal and business register

mnemonic: 옹호 has the 호 of 보호 (protect): you wrap your arms around a cause and speak up for it.

examples.ko: 그는 논란이 된 동료의 발언을 끝까지 옹호했다.
examples.en: He defended his colleague's controversial remarks to the end.

examples.ko: 표현의 자유를 옹호한다고 해서 모든 발언을 용인하자는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Defending free speech doesn't mean tolerating every statement.

production.promptEn: defense / advocacy (speaking up for a person, cause, or position)

mnemonic: 옹립: a group props someone up and stands them (립, as in 설립 'set up') on the throne. 후보로 옹립하다 = to rally behind someone as the candidate.

collocations.en: to rally behind someone as candidate
to set someone on the throne

examples.ko: 당내 비주류 의원들은 그를 차기 대표 후보로 옹립하려는 움직임을 보였다.
examples.en: Lawmakers outside the party mainstream moved to rally behind him as the next leadership candidate.

examples.ko: 어린 왕자를 왕으로 옹립한 대신들이 실권을 쥐었다.
examples.en: The ministers who put the young prince on the throne held the real power.

production.promptEn: installing / rallying behind someone as leader (or monarch)

mnemonic: 비호 has the 호 of 보호, but the one being protected doesn't deserve it: ~의 비호 아래 = under someone's shady protection.

examples.ko: 검찰은 윗선의 비호가 없었다면 이런 비리가 십 년 넘게 계속될 수 없었을 것으로 보고 있다.
examples.en: Prosecutors believe the corruption couldn't have gone on for over ten years without protection from higher up.

examples.ko: 사장이 조카라고 무조건 비호하니까 다른 직원들 불만이 쌓이지.
examples.en: The boss covers for him no matter what because he's his nephew, so of course the rest of the staff are fed up.

production.promptEn: shielding / protecting someone (often a wrongdoer)

mnemonic: 의혹 = 의심 (doubt) + 미혹 (bewilderment): something murky enough that people start asking questions.

examples.ko: 한 언론사가 공사 입찰 과정에서 특혜가 있었다는 의혹을 제기했다.
examples.en: A media outlet raised allegations of favoritism in the construction bidding.

examples.ko: 해명을 하면 할수록 의혹만 커지는 것 같아.
examples.en: The more he explains, the more suspicious it looks.

production.promptEn: suspicion / allegation (publicly raised, e.g., of wrongdoing)

mnemonic: 회의적 = keeping a 의심 tucked inside. Nothing to do with 회의 'meeting': a 회의적 attitude just doubts.

examples.ko: 전문가 대다수는 그 기술이 오 년 안에 상용화될 수 있을지에 대해 회의적이다.
examples.en: Most experts are skeptical that the technology can be commercialized within five years.

examples.ko: 처음엔 나도 회의적이었는데 막상 써 보니까 꽤 괜찮더라.
examples.en: I was skeptical at first too, but once I actually tried it, it was pretty good.

production.promptEn: skeptical

mnemonic: 혐의 is the 의심 that hangs over a suspect: 혐의를 받다 (be suspected), 혐의를 벗다 (be cleared).

collocations.en: to be indicted on charges of …

examples.ko: 그는 회삿돈을 빼돌린 혐의로 구속 기소됐다.
examples.en: He was arrested and indicted on charges of embezzling company funds.

examples.ko: 결국 증거 불충분으로 혐의를 벗긴 했지만 이미지는 이미 망가진 뒤였어요.
examples.en: He was eventually cleared for lack of evidence, but by then his image was already ruined.

production.promptEn: charges; suspicion of having committed an offense

mnemonic: 곤혹 = 곤란 + 당혹: boxed in, with no good answer. What you go through is a different word, 곤욕 (곤욕을 치르다).

examples.ko: 기자의 예상치 못한 질문에 대변인은 곤혹스러운 표정을 지었다.
examples.en: Faced with the reporter's unexpected question, the spokesperson looked at a loss.

examples.ko: 둘 다 내 친구라 누구 편을 들기도 곤혹스러워.
examples.en: They're both my friends, so taking sides puts me in a really awkward spot.

production.promptEn: perplexed and uncomfortable; put on the spot

mnemonic: 현혹: dazzled (현, as in 현기증 'dizziness') and led astray (혹, as in 미혹). Too bright to see straight, so you walk the wrong way.

collocations.en: to be taken in, be dazzled

examples.ko: 고수익을 보장한다는 말에 현혹돼 노후 자금을 날린 사람이 적지 않다.
examples.en: Quite a few people have lost their retirement savings after being lured by promises of guaranteed high returns.

examples.ko: 할인 문구에 현혹되지 말고 원래 가격부터 확인해 봐.
examples.en: Don't be taken in by the sale signs. Check the original price first.

production.promptEn: dazzling / luring into error (being taken in by glitter)

mnemonic: 오 is 'wrong' (오해, 오류); 인 is recognizing (인식): recognizing, but wrongly. A를 B로 오인하다.

examples.ko: 경찰은 피해자를 용의자로 오인해 체포하는 실수를 저질렀다.
examples.en: Police mistook the victim for the suspect and wrongly arrested him.

examples.ko: 고객이 할인 쿠폰을 결제 수단으로 오인할 수 있으니 문구를 고칩시다.
examples.en: Customers might mistake the discount coupon for a payment method, so let's fix the wording.

production.promptEn: mistaking (A for B); misidentification

mnemonic: 오판 = 오 (wrong, as in 오해) + 판단: a judgment gone wrong.

examples.ko: 경영진이 시장 상황을 오판한 탓에 재고가 산더미처럼 쌓였다.
examples.en: Because management misread the market, inventory piled up sky-high.

examples.ko: 그 경기는 심판의 오판 하나로 승부가 갈렸다.
examples.en: That match was decided by a single bad call from the referee.

production.promptEn: a misjudgment; a bad call

mnemonic: 착오 = 착각 + 오류: wires crossed somewhere along the way. 시행착오 = trial and error.

examples.ko: 전산 착오로 일부 고객에게 요금이 두 번 청구됐다.
examples.en: Because of a computer error, some customers were billed twice.

examples.ko: 시행착오를 몇 번 겪고 나서야 우리 팀에 맞는 방식을 찾았어요.
examples.en: It took some trial and error before we found a way of working that suits our team.

production.promptEn: an error / slip (esp. clerical or administrative)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; also in 시행___ (trial and error)

mnemonic: Contracts, licenses, visas: 갱신, a fresh start (think 갱생). Records: 경신, the record changes hands (think 변경).

examples.ko: 집주인이 전세 계약 갱신을 거절하는 바람에 급하게 이사할 집을 구해야 했다.
examples.en: The landlord refused to renew the lease, so I had to find a new place in a hurry.

examples.ko: 운전면허 갱신 기간을 놓쳐서 과태료를 냈어요.
examples.en: I missed the window to renew my driver's license and had to pay a fine.

production.promptEn: renewal (of a contract, license, or visa)

mnemonic: Records are 경신: the record changes (변경) hands. Contracts, licenses, and visas are 갱신.
meanings: setting a new high or low

collocations.en: to set new records day after day

examples.ko: 올여름 서울의 낮 최고 기온이 연일 기록을 경신하고 있다.
examples.en: Seoul's daytime highs are breaking records day after day this summer.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 자기가 세운 세계 기록을 두 달 만에 다시 경신했다.
examples.en: The athlete broke her own world record again just two months later.

production.promptEn: breaking (a record); setting a new high
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; same hanja as the word for renewing a contract, read differently

mnemonic: 전락 = 전환 (turn) + 추락 (fall): rolling over the edge and landing somewhere worse.

collocations.en: to be reduced to, degenerate into

examples.ko: 수백억 원을 들여 지은 경기장이 대회가 끝나자 애물단지로 전락했다.
examples.en: Built for tens of billions of won, the stadium became a white elephant once the games ended.

examples.ko: 한때 업계 일 위였던 회사가 불과 몇 년 만에 하청 업체로 전락했다.
examples.en: Once the industry leader, the company was reduced to a subcontractor within just a few years.

production.promptEn: a fall / being reduced to (a lower, worse state)

mnemonic: 전가 has the 전 of 전환 (shift): you shift blame or costs onto someone else. 책임을 전가하다.

collocations.en: to pass costs on to consumers

examples.ko: 원자재 가격이 오르자 기업들은 그 부담을 소비자에게 전가했다.
examples.en: When raw-material prices rose, companies passed the burden on to consumers.

examples.ko: 사고가 나자 관계 기관들은 서로 책임을 전가하기에 바빴다.
examples.en: After the accident, the agencies involved were busy pinning the blame on each other.

production.promptEn: shifting (blame, responsibility, or costs) onto others

mnemonic: 호전 = a 전환 (turn) toward the good (호감, 호평): 증세가 호전되다, the symptoms improve.

collocations.en: to improve, take a turn for the better

examples.ko: 다행히 수술 후 아버지의 상태가 빠르게 호전되고 있다.
examples.en: Fortunately, my father's condition has been improving quickly since the surgery.

examples.ko: 수출이 늘면서 경기가 호전될 거라는 기대가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: With exports rising, hopes are growing that the economy will pick up.

accepted: take a turn for the better

production.promptEn: improvement; a turn for the better (health, the economy, a situation)

mnemonic: Same spelling root, two words. 일체 = all of it (체, as in 전체 'the whole'): 비용 일체. 일절 = not at all (절, as in 절단 'cut off'), always with a negative.

examples.ko: 행사 참가비에는 식비와 교통비 일체가 포함되어 있습니다.
examples.en: The registration fee covers all meals and transportation.

examples.ko: 이사하면서 살림살이 일체를 새로 장만했다.
examples.en: When we moved, we bought all-new household goods.

production.promptEn: all; everything; the whole (of something)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; 一切 read so that it means 'all of it' (no negative needed)

mnemonic: 절 as in 절단 'cut off': 일절 cuts it off completely (일절 금지). Its twin 일체 (체, as in 전체) means 'all of it'.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 사생활에 관한 질문에는 일절 답하지 않았다.
examples.en: The actor declined to answer any questions whatsoever about her private life.

examples.ko: 회의 중에는 휴대폰 사용을 일절 금합니다.
examples.en: Phone use is strictly prohibited during the meeting.

production.promptEn: (not) at all; absolutely no (with negatives and bans)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adverb; 一切 read so that it means 'none at all'

mnemonic: 유래 = where it comes (래, as in 미래 'what's to come') from (유, as in 이유). Its look-alike 유례 (례, as in 사례 'example') is a precedent.

examples.ko: 이 동네 이름은 옛날 이곳에 있던 큰 나루터에서 유래했다고 한다.
examples.en: They say the neighborhood's name comes from a big ferry landing that used to be here.

examples.ko: 명절 음식 하나하나에도 저마다의 유래가 있다.
examples.en: Even each holiday dish has its own origin story.

production.promptEn: origin, derivation (where something comes from)

mnemonic: 유례 has the 례 of 사례 (example): another example of the same kind. If there's none, it's 유례없다. 유래 (래, as in 미래) is an origin.

examples.ko: 올해 장마는 기상 관측 이래 유례를 찾아보기 힘들 만큼 길었다.
examples.en: This year's monsoon was so long it's hard to find a parallel since records began.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 유례없는 호황 속에서 직원들에게 특별 보너스를 지급했다.
examples.en: Amid an unprecedented boom, the company paid its staff a special bonus.

production.promptEn: a precedent / parallel (usually as 'unprecedented': ___없다)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; NOT the word for 'origin'

mnemonic: 띄다 is 뜨이다 squeezed together: something 뜨이다, comes into view, before your eyes. The sash-wearing 띠다 has no ㅢ.

examples.ko: 회색 정장들 사이에서 그녀의 빨간 코트가 단연 눈에 띄었다.
examples.en: Among all the gray suits, her red coat stood out.

examples.ko: 요즘 들어 동네에 빈 가게가 부쩍 눈에 띄어.
examples.en: Lately you notice a lot more empty shops in the neighborhood.

production.promptEn: to catch the eye; to be noticeable (usually 눈에 ___)
production.contextHint: native verb; NOT the near-homophone 'to take on (a quality)'

mnemonic: 데면데면: two people skimming each other's surfaces, never getting past 'hi'.

examples.ko: 같은 부서에서 삼 년을 일했지만 그 사람과는 아직도 데면데면하다.
examples.en: I've worked in the same department as him for three years, but we're still not close.

examples.ko: 사촌들이랑은 어릴 때 이후로 거의 못 봐서 만나도 좀 데면데면해.
examples.en: I've barely seen my cousins since we were kids, so it's a bit stiff when we meet.

production.promptEn: distant, not close (between people who might be)

mnemonic: 뜬금 is a 'floating price' with no fixed value: a remark that floats in from nowhere.

examples.ko: 회의 도중에 부장님이 뜬금없이 점심 메뉴 얘기를 꺼내셨다.
examples.en: In the middle of the meeting, the department head suddenly brought up what to have for lunch.

examples.ko: 십 년 만에 연락해서 돈 빌려 달라니, 너무 뜬금없지 않아?
examples.en: Getting in touch after ten years to borrow money? Isn't that totally out of the blue?

production.promptEn: out of the blue; random (and out of place)

mnemonic: 에 + 두르다 'wrap around': you wrap your words around the point instead of hitting it.
meanings: to speak in a roundabout way

examples.ko: 그는 제안을 받아들일 수 없다는 뜻을 에둘러 전했다.
examples.en: He conveyed, in a roundabout way, that he couldn't accept the offer.

examples.ko: 에둘러 말하면 못 알아들으니까 그냥 직설적으로 말해 줘.
examples.en: If you hint, I won't get it, so just tell me straight.

production.promptEn: to say something indirectly / in a roundabout way (usually 에둘러 말하다)

mnemonic: 너스레를 떨다: filling the air with chatter so the awkward part slips by unnoticed.

collocations.en: to banter, run one's mouth playfully
to banter with a straight face

examples.ko: 그는 한 시간이나 늦어 놓고도 길이 막힌 게 자기 탓이냐며 너스레를 떨었다.
examples.en: He showed up an hour late and still made light of it, asking if the traffic was his fault.

examples.ko: 너스레 그만 떨고 본론이나 말해.
examples.en: Enough with the banter. Get to the point.

production.promptEn: glib, joking banter (to charm or deflect), as in ___를 떨다

mnemonic: 볼 cheek + 멘 (볼이 메다, cheeks puffed up in a sulk): the voice that comes out of puffed cheeks.

examples.ko: 주말 근무가 잦아지자 직원들 사이에서 볼멘소리가 나오기 시작했다.
examples.en: As weekend shifts became more frequent, grumbling started among the staff.

examples.ko: 동생은 왜 맨날 자기만 설거지를 하냐고 볼멘소리를 했다.
examples.en: My younger brother grumbled about always being the one stuck with the dishes.

production.promptEn: a sulky complaint; grumbling
production.contextHint: native noun; the cheek (볼) is involved

mnemonic: 흐지부지: the hiss of a firework that never goes off.

collocations.en: to be swept under the rug

examples.ko: 요란하게 시작한 조사는 책임자 한 명 가려내지 못한 채 흐지부지 끝났다.
examples.en: The investigation that began with such fanfare petered out without identifying a single person responsible.

examples.ko: 운동 계획 세운 거 또 흐지부지됐어?
examples.en: Did your workout plan fizzle out again?

production.promptEn: fizzling out; inconclusively (ending without result)

mnemonic: Picture someone fanning embers that were already there: 부추기다 feeds a flame, it doesn't light it.

examples.ko: 자극적인 보도가 오히려 시민들의 불안을 부추겼다.
examples.en: Sensational coverage only stoked public anxiety.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 부추기니까 나도 모르게 비싼 걸 사 버렸어.
examples.en: Everyone kept egging me on, so before I knew it I'd bought the expensive one.

production.promptEn: to egg on, incite; to stoke (anxiety, spending, a fight)

mnemonic: 꼬투리 is a bean pod: the critic pries it open, hoping a little seed of fault falls out.

collocations.en: to give someone something to pick at
a slip of the tongue someone seizes on

examples.ko: 그 상사는 보고서 내용보다 맞춤법 하나하나에 꼬투리를 잡는다.
examples.en: That boss nitpicks every little spelling slip instead of engaging with what the report says.

examples.ko: 괜히 꼬투리 잡힐 일 만들지 말고 서류는 꼼꼼히 챙겨.
examples.en: Don't give them anything to pick at. Be thorough with the paperwork.

production.promptEn: a pretext for criticism; something to nitpick (usually ___를 잡다)
production.contextHint: native noun; literally a bean pod

mnemonic: 마뜩하다 'just right' + 않다: not quite right by the speaker's standards.

examples.ko: 아버지는 내가 회사를 그만두고 창업한다는 게 영 마뜩잖으신 눈치였다.
examples.en: Dad seemed none too pleased that I was quitting to start my own business.

examples.ko: 그는 마뜩잖은 표정으로 서류를 훑어보더니 한숨을 쉬었다.
examples.en: He skimmed the documents with a look of displeasure and sighed.

production.promptEn: not to one's liking; displeasing (felt as mild disapproval)
production.contextHint: native adjective; written; a contraction of '___하지 않다'

mnemonic: 짐짓: the little pause before a performance, when you decide to act as if you don't know.

examples.ko: 그는 다 알고 있으면서도 짐짓 모르는 척 고개를 갸웃했다.
examples.en: He knew everything, yet he cocked his head as if he had no idea.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손주들 앞에서 짐짓 엄한 목소리를 냈지만 입가에는 웃음이 번져 있었다.
examples.en: Grandma put on a stern voice for the grandkids, but a smile was spreading across her lips.

production.promptEn: deliberately, feigning (putting on a show of something)

mnemonic: 되레 is 도리어 with the middle swallowed: same reversal, faster delivery.

collocations.en: to bluster when one is in the wrong

examples.ko: 잘못한 쪽이 되레 큰소리를 치니 기가 막힌다.
examples.en: The one who's in the wrong is the one yelling. Unbelievable.

examples.ko: 다이어트한다고 굶었더니 되레 살이 쪘어.
examples.en: I starved myself to lose weight and put it on instead.

production.promptEn: instead; on the contrary (the opposite of what you'd expect)
production.contextHint: native adverb; short form of 도리어, common in speech and headlines

mnemonic: 미적미적: someone shuffling sideways toward a task they'd rather not face.

collocations.en: to drag one's feet on a decision

examples.ko: 정부가 대책 발표를 미적거리는 사이 피해는 눈덩이처럼 불어났다.
examples.en: While the government dragged its feet on announcing measures, the damage snowballed.

examples.ko: 미적거리지 말고 빨리 신청서 내. 오늘 마감이야.
examples.en: Stop dawdling and get the application in. It's due today.

production.promptEn: to dawdle; drag one's feet (on a decision or task)

mnemonic: Picture a single candle flame: whole, upright, nothing split off. That's 오롯이.

examples.ko: 아이를 재우고 난 뒤의 한 시간은 오롯이 나만을 위한 시간이다.
examples.en: The hour after I put the kids to bed is wholly my own.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 원작의 쓸쓸한 정서를 화면에 오롯이 담아냈다.
examples.en: The film captures the novel's lonely mood on screen, whole and undiminished.

production.promptEn: wholly, fully (undivided, all to itself)
